question: What is the primary purpose of the pulmonary circulation system?

options.A: To deliver nutrient-rich blood directly to the brain
options.B: To pump blood against a very high vascular resistance
options.C: To filter waste products out of systemic blood vessels
options.D: To exchange carbon dioxide for oxygen in the lungs

explanation: The primary function of pulmonary circulation is to move blood through the lungs so carbon dioxide can be dropped off and fresh oxygen picked up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: How does pulmonary circulation differ from systemic circulation?

options.A: Pulmonary circulation bypasses the right side of the heart
options.B: Pulmonary circulation operates under much lower pressure
options.C: Systemic circulation only carries deoxygenated blood
options.D: Systemic circulation has a shorter pathway than pulmonary

explanation: The pulmonary circuit is a low-pressure pathway because the lungs are close to the heart and offer less resistance than the entire systemic body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which heart chamber pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk?
explanation: The right ventricle is responsible for forcing deoxygenated blood out of the heart and into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: What makes pulmonary arteries unique compared to most other arteries in the body?

options.A: They operate under very high pressure
options.C: They contain multiple valves to prevent backflow
options.D: They transport blood toward the body organs

explanation: While almost all other arteries carry oxygenated blood to the body, pulmonary arteries are unique because they carry deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: What valve does blood pass through immediately after leaving the right ventricle?
explanation: As the right ventricle contracts, blood pushes open the pulmonary semilunar valve to enter the pulmonary trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: A patient has a blockage right at the entrance of the pulmonary trunk. Which chamber of the heart will struggle to empty its blood first?
explanation: The right ventricle pumps directly into the pulmonary trunk, so a blockage there creates backpressure and makes it hard for the right ventricle to empty. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: How do oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the alveolar-capillary membrane?
explanation: Gases move naturally across the thin membrane from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration without using cellular energy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: What happens to carbon dioxide during gas exchange in the lungs?

options.A: It moves from the pulmonary capillaries into the alveoli
options.B: It combines with oxygen to form a new nutrient compound
options.C: It binds tightly to hemoglobin inside the red blood cells
options.D: It is actively pumped from the alveoli into the bloodstream

explanation: Carbon dioxide travels from the blood in the capillaries across the membrane into the air sacs so it can leave the body through exhalation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which heart chamber receives oxygenated blood directly from the pulmonary veins?
explanation: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood back from the lungs and empty it straight into the left atrium of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: How many pulmonary veins normally return oxygenated blood to the heart?
explanation: There are typically four pulmonary veins in total, with two coming from each lung. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why is blood pressure in the pulmonary circulation much lower than in systemic circulation?

options.A: To protect delicate lung tissues and prevent fluid buildup
options.B: Because the right ventricle is much stronger than the left
options.C: To slow down red blood cells so they can produce more energy
options.D: Because the lungs require very little blood flow to survive

explanation: Lower pressure in the pulmonary circuit prevents excess fluid from leaking into the delicate air sacs of the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: How do pulmonary blood vessels react to an area of the lung that lacks proper ventilation?

options.A: They constrict to redirect blood to better ventilated areas
options.B: They burst open to release stored oxygen reserves into the tissue
options.C: They dilate to force more blood into the poorly ventilated alveoli
options.D: They completely shut down the entire right side of the heart

explanation: Pulmonary vessels automatically constrict in poorly ventilated areas, ensuring blood is sent to parts of the lung where oxygen is actually available. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the medical term for right-sided heart failure caused by long-term high blood pressure in the pulmonary vessels?
explanation: Cor pulmonale refers to enlargement and failure of the right ventricle resulting from chronic disorders within the pulmonary arterial system. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)

question: A patient suddenly develops severe shortness of breath and chest pain after a long plane ride. Which condition should the nurse suspect first?
explanation: Immobility during a long trip can lead to blood clots in the legs that break off and travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)
